title: Fail closed when Terminal has no command authorizer
goal: Prevent terminal commands from running when no TerminalCommandAuthorizing policy has been supplied.
context: CommandRegistry.isAuthorized currently returns true when its optional authorizer is nil. The production Terminal screen wires SettingsTerminalCommandAuthorizer after sandbox setup, but the reusable terminal API itself defaults to allow-all and can bypass the Settings authorization boundary when constructed incorrectly.
forbidden_changes: Do not change the production SettingsTerminalCommandAuthorizer or grant new capabilities.
Do not change terminal command capability classification.
Do not treat missing authorization as an implicit grant.
acceptance_criteria: CommandRegistry.isAuthorized returns false when no authorizer is injected.
Executing a known command without an authorizer returns a permission-denied result and performs no mutation.
Tests that intentionally exercise command handlers inject an explicit test authorizer.
Production TerminalScreen remains wired to SettingsTerminalCommandAuthorizer.
verification: Check Swift package tests + repository integrity and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA CI.
recovery: Revert the single task commit if a terminal command unexpectedly mutates without authorization or required CI fails.
